clue.text: Gatehouse

parts.note: split as gate plus house: a sports crowd is the gate, a theatre crowd is the house, and one word covers both

explanation.surface: A single word naming the lodge at the entrance to an estate.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue looks like a building, but read it as two words: a 'gate' is the paying crowd at a match, and a 'house' is the people watching a play.
explanation.definitionFit: Both gate and house are words for the spectators gathered at an event, the crowd watching.

clue.text: Responsibility lies with you and me

parts.note: a duty that lies with someone is on them
you and me together are us

explanation.surface: Someone pointing out that a duty falls to the two of them.
explanation.definitionFit: An onus is a burden or duty, a close synonym for responsibility.

clue.text: A place of opportunity?

parts.note: an opening or route you might pursue, figuratively a road leading to chances, and literally a street

explanation.surface: A question about where chances are to be found.
explanation.walkthrough: We speak of exploring every possible line of approach as a street to go down, so a broad tree-lined road doubles as a figurative opportunity.
explanation.definitionFit: A promising line of approach is often called a way forward, and also a broad road in a town.

clue.text: Virtuous pope

definitions.meaning: free from guilt or sin, blameless
thirteen popes have taken this name, including the third of that name who called the Fourth Lateran Council

explanation.surface: A description of a saintly pontiff.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means guiltless, and it is also the papal name borne by thirteen popes.

clue.text: Clean — very odd round about September 1

indicators.note: the word for very odd goes round the other pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: antic as an adjective means grotesque, bizarre
the digit one looks like the letter I
Sept is the standard short form of September

explanation.surface: A remark that something hygienic is strange around the start of autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: Antic is an old adjective for grotesque or bizarre; the digit 1 stands for the letter I, which lands just before SEPT inside the enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that kills germs is clean in the sense of sterile and free from infection.

clue.text: Food for father and others outside

indicators.note: the word for others sits outside the word for father, wrapping it

parts.note: the rest means the others, the remainder
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A meal prepared for dad and the rest of the family, eaten out of doors.
explanation.definitionFit: A repast is a meal, so food in the sense of something eaten.

clue.text: Buying and selling, as the reader might

definitions.meaning: the volume of trade a business does over a period
what someone reading does to get to the next page

explanation.surface: A comparison between trading and someone leafing through a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Turnover is a firm's total sales, and to turn over is what a reader does to a page.

clue.text: Motive concerning an endless strain

parts.note: re is a Latin-derived word meaning about or concerning

indicators.note: the last letter of the word for strain is dropped

parts.note: a strain is a tune, a song

explanation.surface: A suggestion that someone's motive relates to an unfinished tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts the G from SONG, leaving SON.
explanation.definitionFit: A reason is the cause behind an action, a direct synonym for a motive.

clue.text: St Anne re-located in France

indicators.note: moved to a new place, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A saint's shrine being moved somewhere in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Nantes is a city on the Loire in western France, so it is a place found there.

clue.text: Fail to notice lady teacher

definitions.meaning: a schoolchild's way of addressing a woman teacher

explanation.surface: A pupil's careless teacher who overlooks things.
explanation.definitionFit: To miss something is to overlook it, and pupils address a woman teacher by that title.

clue.text: Ice cream mixture — a pint alone

indicators.note: a mixture blends things together, so the letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A dessert blend made from a pint of something on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Neapolitan is the three-striped ice cream of chocolate, vanilla and strawberry.

clue.text: Before embracing NCO once more

indicators.note: the word for before holds the abbreviation in its arms

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: A soldier hugged before being asked to come back again.
explanation.walkthrough: NCO, a non-commissioned officer such as a sergeant, is given as printed, and the surface tempts you to read 'Before' as the start of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Encore is the French for again, used in English when an audience calls for more.

clue.text: Grievances concerning nice jobs to swap

indicators.note: the letters change places with each other

explanation.surface: Complaints arising over a proposal to exchange good positions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concerning' is a link; 'to' belongs to the fodder, giving the T and second O.
explanation.definitionFit: Objections are protests raised against something, much like complaints or grievances.

clue.text: Some letters describe how to cook this dish

definitions.text: Some letters describe how to cook this dish

indicators.note: to describe is to trace round, so the two words encircle the dish's name within their run of letters

explanation.surface: A recipe set out in a few written lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some letters' looks like the start of a recipe card, but the dish runs through those two words; 'describe' in its old sense of drawing round something signals the enclosure, and the whole clue is also the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a classic folded dish of beaten eggs, and a few written lines can explain how it is cooked.

clue.text: Encourage Jonnie indecently

indicators.note: the name is treated improperly, so its letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Someone urging a man called Jonnie on in an improper way.
explanation.definitionFit: To enjoin is to urge or direct someone to do something, close to encouraging them.

clue.text: Television shows fool sitting on case

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: an idiot is a fool
a box is a case or container

explanation.surface: A TV set showing a clown perched on a crate.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiot box is a slang, mildly scornful name for a television set.

clue.text: University head in the country, being unable to move

indicators.note: the first letter goes inside the word for the country

parts.note: a state is a country or nation

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A university head stuck at home, unable to get about.
explanation.definitionFit: A statue is a sculpted figure, a being fixed in place that cannot move.

clue.text: Tom, Dick or Harry wants poor Mary in uniform

indicators.note: the jumbled name goes inside the word for uniform

parts.note: even means regular or uniform

indicators.note: poor suggests the name is in bad shape, so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A man seeking poor Mary, who is dressed in uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom, Dick or Harry' means any ordinary man, the medieval morality play's hero; 'wants' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Every Tom, Dick or Harry is the ordinary person, as is the archetypal common man of the medieval morality play.

clue.text: Fungus that could be rolled into a cigar

indicators.note: rolling the letters about forms them into a new word

explanation.surface: A mushroom that might be wrapped up inside a cigar.
explanation.definitionFit: Agaric is the name for a gilled mushroom or toadstool, a kind of fungus.

clue.text: Complaining because bishop's very eager

parts.note: B is the chess notation for a bishop; the 's is a link
itching means very keen to do something

explanation.surface: Someone grumbling because a bishop is impatient to act.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitching is a slang word for complaining spitefully or moaning.

clue.text: Definitely, Sally and I are to be converted

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: converting something changes its form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A declaration that Sally and the speaker will both undergo a religious conversion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' joins the two parts of the fodder and gives no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is an emphatic yes, meaning certainly or definitely.

clue.text: Angel in support

definitions.meaning: in theatre, an angel is a financial investor in a show
a supporter, someone who stands behind a cause

explanation.surface: A heavenly being offering help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Angel' is theatrical slang for someone who puts money into a production; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A backer is a financial sponsor of a show and, more generally, a supporter of a cause.

clue.text: Old dagger for person with family

parts.note: bod is British slang for a person
kin are one's relatives, one's family

explanation.surface: An antique knife meant for someone with relatives.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodkin was once a short pointed dagger, the sense Hamlet uses in his soliloquy.

clue.text: Secluded tree is cold like this

indicators.note: the fodder letters are made to look like the definition, so rearranged into it

explanation.surface: A tree described as cold because it is cut off from others.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloistered means shut away from the world, as monks are in a cloister, hence secluded.

clue.text: What may be in this sauce? May a duck's egg

parts.note: taken as written
in cricket a duck is a score of nought, so a duck's egg is the round letter O

explanation.surface: A question about whether a duck's egg could go into this dressing.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman out for no runs scores a duck, from the egg shape of the zero. The whole clue also hints that egg yolk is a key ingredient.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayo is the short informal name for mayonnaise, an egg-based sauce.

clue.text: Chap eats nothing but beef

indicators.note: the word for chap takes the other letter inside itself

parts.note: a chap is a man
nothing is zero, shown as the letter O

explanation.surface: A man who eats nothing except beef.
explanation.definitionFit: Beef as a verb is slang for complain, so it means the same as grumble.

clue.text: A bingo game in a brothel!

indicators.note: game in the sense of lame or crooked, so the letters are out of line

explanation.surface: A round of bingo being played in a house of ill repute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a' is a link between the wordplay and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A bagnio is an old word for a bathhouse that came to mean a house of prostitution.

clue.text: An oriental bowl?

parts.note: bowl as a verb, a delivery in cricket, versus bowl as a dish of porcelain from the East

explanation.surface: A question about a dish from the Far East.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket this is a left-arm wrist-spinner's delivery. The surface suggests a porcelain dish; the word itself is now regarded as offensive for a Chinese person.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names a left-arm unorthodox spin delivery in cricket, a kind of ball bowled.
